A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LALNet, with matching authors, research objectives, and benchmark coverage. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LALNet benchmark results, component and loss ablations, and third-party HDR image/video evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original results for the revised LALNet, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and appendix generalization evaluations.

M1.justification: V1's two-stream VSSM is replaced by LSSM: color-separated features are added before projection and processed through an additional SS2D stream that joins the mixed-feature stream (v2 Section 3.3.2, Equations 11-13). This changes the computational pathway substantially. WFM's renaming to MCM retains essentially the same wavelet construction, and the aggregate loss retains its four named terms.

E1.justification: Both evaluate exposure correction, image retouching, low-light enhancement, and tone mapping using SCIE, HDR+, LOL-v1, and HDRI Haven. MSEC and the test-only HDR Survey and UVTM image/video evaluations already appear in v1 Appendix D and remain in v2 Appendix C. No additional dataset or test scenario is established.

E2.justification: The HDR+ quantitative comparison adds MambaIR and removes UPE and LPTN. The LOL comparison adds Diff-Retinex and DiffIR while removing 3DLUT and CSRNet rows; CSRNet remains in the qualitative comparison. MSEC drops LIME. SCIE and tone-mapping comparator membership otherwise remains unchanged, making these limited revisions to the existing comparison sets.

E3.justification: V2 changes the stated initial learning rate from 0.0002 to 0.0001, adds NIQE evaluation on SCIE and HDR+, and substantially redesigns component-ablation controls with an explicitly labeled SCIE setting. Evaluated model sizes change from 2.87M to 2.45M parameters and from 246K to 230K for Tiny; Lite is omitted. Dataset splits and the 400,000-iteration training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 Table 4's loss-function ablation is removed. The component study is substantially revised: v2 Table 5 includes an all-residual baseline and explicit LSSM removal, replacing v1's five-condition study. Pyramid-depth, attention/residual replacement, group-convolution, motivation, and third-party generalization analyses remain; their relocation alone does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or statistical significance tests. Both primarily present single metric values; uses of 'significantly' do not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: Full-model PSNR changes from 30.36 to 30.24 on HDR+, 23.70 to 23.80 on SCIE average, 25.29 to 25.26 on LOL, and 32.28 to 32.46 on HDRI Haven. These accompany model and training changes, so are not controlled performance gains or losses. NIQE and new comparator results are added, Lite and loss-ablation results disappear, and numerous appendix values change. V2's MSEC table reports 23.90/0.8713/0.0801, while its prose retains v1's 23.93/0.8734/0.0791.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification changes locally: state-space feature equations are revised, while explicit definitions of DDCM's softmax reweighting and the multiscale reconstruction/high-frequency losses are removed. V2 still uses the primed Fourier components without defining their reweighting. Neither version contains a theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The central claim remains one channel-aware architecture applied separately to four lighting tasks with strong accuracy and modest computation. Headline advantage claims are recalibrated: HDR+ superiority changes from 3.55 dB over RetinexMamba to 2.15 dB over the newly included MambaIR. The abstract also highlights LSSM, but does not establish a new joint-training claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds a mechanism explanation for LSSM: fusing global information from separated and mixed features is argued to improve sensitivity to lighting conditions. V1 described VSSM primarily through long-range dependency modeling. Interpretation of the removed loss ablation disappears, while the channel-interference, pyramid-depth, and generalization arguments largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's Gaussian/Laplacian loss-target details, VGG19 layer specification, detailed learnable differential pyramid construction, and cosine-decay schedule. Appendix E retains only loss names and their weighted sum. V2 newly describes Tiny as using fewer channels and blocks, but the overall implementation documentation is substantially reduced. The demo hyperlink retains the same target; no new resource availability is established.

R1.justification: V2 newly credits the differential pyramid to Yang et al. (2024) and adds references including consistency modeling, DiffIR, and Diff-Retinex. References associated with removed discussion or comparisons, including FiveK, LIME, and VGG, disappear. The broad positioning around shared lighting properties remains; moving related work into the main text is a structural change.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, loss functions move from Section 2.5 to a condensed Appendix E, and task presentation is reordered. The abstract, related-work discussion, and state-space explanation are rewritten. Main-text terminology largely changes from 'time domain' to 'spatial domain,' and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, rearranges Figure 1 into a two-by-two grid, redraws the architecture and detail-enhancement diagrams, removes the differential-pyramid diagram, and adds an LSSM diagram. Tone-mapping and LOL tables move into the main text, HDR+ visual comparisons move to the appendix, and table structures change through NIQE and revised ablation columns.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, NIQE measurements, and the LSSM diagram strengthen evaluation and exposition. However, v2 loses substantial self-contained implementation and loss information from v1 Section 2.5 and Appendix C, leaves Fourier reweighting variables undefined, removes the loss ablation, and introduces disagreement between the MSEC prose and Table 7. These losses in reproducibility and reporting consistency outweigh the limited gains.
